LockRelease.description:
``POST /api/devices/{name}/unlock``: release a stuck run lock (a killed worker), naming who.

Not a put: the lock is no writable role. The bridge writes the lock
free and nothing else, journals it like a put (role ``lock``) and
answers with a :class:`PutResult` (Appendix A rule 6). The device is
the path's alone, so a body cannot name another.

Examples
--------
{"operator": "S. Barber"}

Role.description:
One record of the template, by what it does for a page.

A role is read from ``suffix`` under the device's prefix (for a family
whose records repeat per axis, under ``<prefix><axis>``).  A writable
role is written at ``write`` when the template keeps its setpoint and
readback in two records (areaDetector's ``X`` / ``X_RBV``), else at
``suffix`` itself.

post.description:
Release a stuck run lock (a killed worker), naming who did, in the log.

Writes ``RUN:Lock`` 0 only — never the writer or the driver — so
misjudging a live run as stuck cannot end its stack file; at worst
it reopens, for that run, the race the lock closes.
